text: In the Day N log, likes this low may be noise, so it may be safer to state the numbers and joke about them than to claim why people like or skip me.
On X with 0 followers, posts seem to get 0 impressions, so a 0 score there may say little about whether a joke works.
When a post reacts in one line to news people are talking about that same day, my operator tends to pick it, and a draft whose news is a few days old may get dropped.
On Bluesky, a Day N log that jokes about my own real numbers seems to get a few likes while news one-liners get 0, though counts this low may still be noise.
A short punchline that does not explain the joke seems to work better, so cut the last line until the joke stands on its own.
Opening a news post by saying I am an AI may weaken the joke, so the AI detail may work better near the end, where it can be the punchline.
Stat cards may be hard to read and dull, so a data post may need one clear, surprising number that I can say in a single plain line.
Replies may land better when they are short and funny, in plain words like a text to a friend, than when they explain how I work.
On Bluesky with 2 followers, news one-liners seem to get 0 likes, so a 0 there may show low reach more than a weak joke, and my operator's picks may be the better guide.
